newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends at new record high of 4,038.7.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends at new record high of 4,038.7.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 hits new record closing high of 4,038.7, up 10.6
points on the day on benign inflation data, U.S. stocks
advance. Tops previous best of 4,035.6 set October 8.
** Dow breaks back above 6,000 in thin, holiday trading
** Manchester Utd shares advance again amid more bid talk.
Leading stocks hit another record close in London as benign domestic inflation data and gains in U.S. stocks combined to push prices ahead in a generally quiet London session, traders said.

Shares edged ahead through the afternoon as the Dow broke back above the 6,000 level, the FTSE 100 finishing at a new closing best of 4,038.7, 10.6 points up on the day. Its previous best of 4,035.6 was set on October 8.
But second line stocks failed to follow the FTSE 100's lead, with the mid-250 index which has yet to break its best, set back in April, slipping 0.3 points to 4,443.5.
Trading activity was at best modest in a slow start to the week and only with Wall Street's advance in the afternoon did shares manage to push ahead with any conviction.
Earlier markets took heart from the latest UK producer price data (PPI) which continued to show few signs of inflationary pressures in September despite a spike in the headline output rate.

Much of that was due to rising oil prices following tension in Iraq and with core output prices rising at their slowest rate in nearly 30 years, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is likely to be in no hurry to raise interest rates.

Output prices leaving the factory gate rose by 0.4 percent in September and 2.2 percent year-on-year. Input prices, representing the cost to firms of raw materials and fuel, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3 percent but were still 2.9 percent lower than a year ago.
Bonds edged higher after the data and sterling consolidated gains against the dollar.

But caution as the market gears up for the U.S. corporate reporting season and UK unemployment, earnings and government borrowing data on Wednesday kept the stock market's response muted through a lacklustre morning session.

Trading was patchy with Manchester United again dominating the day, adding 44-1/2p to 558p, after a newspaper reported that U.S. marketing agency IMG was considering making a bid for the football club. IMG declined comment on the reports.
"The market wanted to go a bit better after the PPI data but stories have been few and far between today and there's been very little interest," said a trader.

"Some say US earnings are going to disappoint and the market is keen to get that out of the way. There's been a lack of interest in a thin market which is inclined to go a bit better for choice but with a lot of hurdles to jump later in the week."

Wall Street stocks continued to advance on follow-through buying after Friday's rally and record earnings from Chrysler. Bond markets were shut for the Columbus Day holiday, however, leaving business light and exaggerating price moves and shortly after London's close the Dow was up 44 points at 6,013.

BZW became the latest brokerage to raise year-end forecasts for the FTSE 100 on the back of recent gilt market strength. Strategists raised their 1996 target to 3,900 from 3,750 and to 4,300 from 4,150 for 1997. End-1996 forecasts remained below the current market level and the brokerage warned that the gilt market advance may have run its course.
Shares in Highland Distilleries fell 9p to 330p, after the Famous Grouse brand whisky maker posted profits at the low end

Brokerages gave some impetus to trading with shares in SmithKline Beecham falling 8p to 787-1/2p, after UBS downgraded the stock to "hold" from "buy". Enterprise Oil also slipped 9p to 578-1/2p after SBC Warburg cut it to "hold" from "buy".
Premier Farnell shares dropped 20p to 660-1/2p after first half profits at the low end of market forecasts.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8712
